summary: Research and fact-check real-world AI use in the 60 handbook departments, by cluster

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All ten departments work mostly with long, unstructured, high-stakes documents (board papers, contracts, filings, case files, deal data rooms), so the shared AI pattern is summarise, compare, extract and draft, with a named human accountable for the output. The sources agree on the same controls: use approved enterprise tools, treat outputs as claims to verify (COSO's framing), keep an inventory of use cases, and scale human review to risk. Shared risks are privilege waiver and discoverability of AI transcripts, material non-public information and deal confidentiality, personal data in investigations (GDPR, whistleblower protections), and AI output that cannot be traced for audit or assurance. Evidence is thinnest for Office of the CEO, ERM and Ethics, where findings come from practitioner or vendor pieces rather than studies. Train together on a common module covering data classification, verification and prompt/output logging, with joint labs for Board Secretariat, Legal and Compliance (records and privilege), for Compliance, Internal Audit and ERM (controls evidence and COSO), and for Corporate Strategy and Corporate Development (scenario and deal analysis).

departments.name: Office of the CEO
ai_use_cases: Executive assistant use of Microsoft 365 Copilot to summarise meetings and materials, plan the week and prepare client meetings; at EY Oceania this made leadership meetings more efficient and nearly 70% of 9,000 staff adopted the tool [1]
Real-time meeting summaries with agreements, disagreements and suggested actions, so executives can leave a meeting and catch up on return [1]

Drafting and summarising communications and reports, and analysing data in Outlook, Teams, Word and Excel, taught through role-specific 1:1 training at a global manufacturer (the specific apps and tasks are not verified on the opened page) [2]
Drafting a first cut of a difficult conversation or message, which the executive then rewrites in their own voice [1]

Selecting a small number of high-impact use cases tied to business goals, with a roadmap and KPIs, as a CEO-CIO joint task (2023 commentary, background only; page opened, specifics not individually checked) [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A weekly CEO briefing pack for one real (or anonymised) week: a one-page decision brief, a KPI narrative with every figure traced to its source, and a meeting-decision log. Submit the documented prompts, the verification checklist showing each number checked against source, and a measured before/after time log (target: at least 40% reduction against a baseline week). Sized for Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Board and strategy papers, unannounced results and deals (material non-public information under securities rules), personal data of executives and staff (GDPR), and privileged legal advice. Rules: use only the licensed enterprise assistant inside the tenant; never paste MNPI into public tools; recorded meetings need consent and a retention rule; the executive office owns verification of every number before it reaches the CEO.
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of executive-office staff using the approved assistant weekly; hours saved per weekly briefing against baseline; share of briefs with all figures source-checked; number of decision-log entries completed within 24 hours of the meeting.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on hands-on drafting and summarising in Microsoft 365 Copilot (the tool leaders actually have in Outlook and Teams), then Claude or Gemini for long-document synthesis, with one short block on verifying numbers. Power BI Copilot only if the office owns KPI dashboards. Concurrency's case shows short, role-specific 1:1 sessions helped executive adoption [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well; Microsoft 365 Copilot is the strongest fit given the cited executive deployments [1][2]. Gamma and ChatGPT Enterprise are optional extras for this function. No opened source names a widely used omitted tool, so omissions are not verified. Source [3] is from 2023, so use it for background only.

departments.name: Corporate Strategy
ai_use_cases: Generating multiple scenarios quickly from financial data, news, filings and customer sentiment, instead of weeks of spreadsheet modelling [1]
Dynamic, updatable scenario models, including unconventional outcomes that human planners filter out [1]
Market and competitive analysis from news, financial reports and industry data, such as generative-search SWOT prompts [2]
Strategic risk simulation of downturns, supply-chain disruption and competitive threats to build contingency plans (supply-chain and downturn specifics not individually verified) [2]
Idea validation: Nestle's proprietary genAI tool cut product ideation from six months to six weeks (as reported by AlphaSense) [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A strategy memo with a three-scenario analysis for one real or case-study market question. Include a source table where every external claim is checked against an original document, the prompt log, and a short note on where the AI view was challenged or corrected, plus time saved against a manual estimate. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unreleased strategy, M&A intentions and competitor analysis that may be material non-public information; third-party licensed research whose terms may restrict AI use; and possible antitrust issues if competitor data is gathered improperly. Rules: no MNPI in non-enterprise tools; cite only opened primary sources; label model-generated assumptions as such.
departments.adoption_kpis: Scenarios produced per planning cycle; days from question to first draft memo; share of memo claims with verified citations; number of AI-surfaced scenarios adopted into plans.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Perplexity Enterprise (sourced research), Claude (long-document synthesis and structured scenario writing), Power BI Copilot (data-backed scenarios) and Gamma only for final board decks. Put the most hours on verification: a BCG experiment cited by AlphaSense found a 23% performance drop on business problem-solving, mainly because participants trusted misleading outputs [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits. Having both Perplexity and Perplexity Enterprise is redundant for corporate use. AlphaSense is cited as a strategy-specific research platform that the handbook omits [2], though it is a vendor source. Gamma is a weak fit for analysis (it is presentation only).

departments.name: Corporate Development & M&A
ai_use_cases: Reviewing every document in a data room, extracting key provisions and flagging non-standard terms into structured reports within hours rather than weeks (vendor claim) [2]
Cross-referencing obligations across thousands of contracts in due diligence [2]
Use across the deal life cycle: 49% of surveyed organisations apply GenAI in deal closing and 52% in post-close integration [1]
90% of surveyed M&A organisations use GenAI, 37% across multiple stages [1]
Document classification and report generation for lawyers to review, with the judgement on risk left to humans [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A due-diligence summary for a sample (public or synthetic) data room of at least 20 contracts: an extraction table of key terms, a red-flag list with page-level citations, an assumptions log for valuation inputs, and a first integration tracker. Submit prompts, a verification sample (at least 20% of extracted items checked by hand with error rate reported) and time saved. Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Material non-public information, target confidential data under NDA, competitively sensitive data (antitrust and gun-jumping limits before closing; clean-team rules), personal data in HR files (GDPR), and legal privilege. Rules: use only the deal-approved data-room or enterprise tool; confirm vendor does not train on deal data; keep human review of high-stakes outputs, which Deloitte's survey names as the top requirement [1]. No opened source covers clean teams or gun-jumping, so those points are general practice, not verified.
departments.adoption_kpis: Documents reviewed per analyst-hour; diligence cycle time to first red-flag report; error rate found in sampled AI extractions; share of deals using an approved AI workflow.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Datasite AI (data-room extraction; capability not verified by an opened source), Claude and NotebookLM (long-document analysis with citations), and Microsoft 365 Copilot for trackers. Spend most Specialist hours on verification design and confidentiality controls, since Deloitte finds integration with approved deal data sources is the most important tool capability [1].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Datasite AI is plausible but not verified by an opened source. The handbook omits legal-diligence platforms such as Harvey, which its own vendor page describes for data-room review [2] (vendor source, treat claims with care). Gemini and ChatGPT Enterprise are generic and only suitable if deal-data terms are cleared.

departments.name: Board Secretariat & Corporate Governance
ai_use_cases: Summarising board materials to highlight key information; Nasdaq added Azure OpenAI summarisation to Boardvantage in 2024 [3]
Distilling lengthy board papers into clear summaries and supporting agenda planning [1]
Drafting board minutes from meetings, with human cross-checking before circulation [1]
Administration: summarising meetings, transcripts, notes and board packs, plus regulatory scanning and alerts [2]
Drafting routine narrative sections of the annual report, with a warning that generic AI text may not reflect company-specific risks [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A mock board pack and minutes set: AI-drafted summary of three board papers, draft minutes from a supplied transcript, and an action register, plus a one-page AI-use policy stating what counts as the official minute, where AI drafts are stored and when they are deleted. Include prompts, a line-by-line accuracy check against the transcript, and time saved. Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Board deliberations, MNPI, privileged legal advice and director personal data (GDPR). AI transcripts and summaries raise questions about which document is the official record, retention and later disclosure in litigation; the claim that sharing AI output beyond the core group risks waiving privilege is not verified from an opened page. Governance bodies advise that AI use sit within policies on accountability and content ownership [4]. Rules: define the formal minutes, restrict who receives AI output, and exclude privileged sessions from AI recording.
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours to produce a board pack; days from meeting to approved minutes; number of corrections found in AI-drafted minutes; share of secretariat staff trained and following the AI-use policy.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Microsoft Teams Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot (meeting capture and drafting), Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant (searching PDF board packs; not verified by an opened source) and Claude for long-paper summaries. Most time should go to record-keeping rules and verification, because the risk lies in minutes and privilege, not drafting speed.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits, but omits dedicated board-portal AI (for example Nasdaq Boardvantage) [3], which is where many boards already keep their papers. NotebookLM is useful for document search but its enterprise data terms should be checked before board material goes in (not verified). Gemini and Claude are general tools and need secure-tenant approval.

departments.name: Enterprise Risk Management
ai_use_cases: Mapping GenAI risks to the existing control framework: COSO's 2026 guidance organises uses by capability, such as data extraction and ingestion and insight generation, with owners assigned per capability [1][2]
Maintaining an inventory of AI use cases with ownership and escalation, including detecting shadow AI [1]
Continuous monitoring of AI performance through indicators such as transaction volume, size and override percentages to detect model drift [1]
Treating AI output as a claim to validate rather than a fact, with risk assessment and change control moving toward continuous [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: An AI-assisted risk register extract: 15 risks for one business unit drafted from supplied policies and incident notes, each with cause, impact, control mapping and owner, plus a trend summary. Include prompts, a reviewer sign-off on each risk, a comparison of AI versus manual drafting time, and a mapping of the team's own AI use cases to COSO's six steps (govern, inventory, assess, design, implement, monitor). Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Incident records, loss data, third-party and cyber vulnerability information, and risk appetite, which may include MNPI and personal data (GDPR). Rules: risk entries remain owned by named humans; no sensitive vulnerability detail in non-enterprise tools; log prompts and approvals so the AI-assisted register can itself be audited (SOX relevance where it supports internal control over financial reporting is general practice, not verified from an opened source).
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to refresh the risk register per cycle; share of risks with mapped controls and owners; number of AI use cases in the inventory with a risk rating; override or correction rate on AI-drafted entries.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude and Microsoft 365 Copilot (drafting and classifying risk text from documents), ServiceNow Now Assist if the firm's risk register lives in ServiceNow, and Power BI Copilot for trend narratives. Give extra time to the COSO six-step roadmap [1][2], since ERM will own AI risk governance.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Broadly fits. ServiceNow Now Assist is only a good fit where ServiceNow GRC is the system of record (no opened source confirms this). Gemini is generic. No opened source names a widely used omitted ERM tool; not verified.

departments.name: Legal Affairs
ai_use_cases: Lease and contract summaries: extraction templates run across a contract folder, then attorney review, to find critical terms and deadlines [1]
Litigation support: locating operative clauses, building chronologies from correspondence, spotting notice defects, turning a day-long first pass into a focused review [1]
Deposition transcript analysis with page-line citations and inconsistency flags, treated as draft work product [1]
Tabular reviews of contracts and production sets as a more advanced stage once workflows are tested (not individually verified) [1]
Starting with lower-risk repetitive tasks (summaries, first-pass review) under an AI-use policy with mandatory attorney review [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A clause-comparison and contract-summary pack for five sample contracts against a playbook: extraction table, deviations list, suggested redlines, with every citation checked against the source, a hallucination log, and an AI-use policy page covering privilege and confidentiality. Include prompts and time saved against manual review. Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Attorney-client privilege and work product, confidential client and company information, personal data (GDPR) and trade secrets. In an ACC global survey of in-house counsel, 56% believed AI tools could compromise privilege and generative AI was seen as the highest-risk category (49%) [2]. Rules: approved enterprise tools with contractual limits on data use, retention and training; review vendor terms (ABA Formal Opinion 512, 2024) [1]; never rely on AI legal research without verification, because of hallucinated citations [1]; obtain consent before putting client data into insufficiently protected tools [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Contract review turnaround time; share of AI outputs with all citations verified; number of privilege or confidentiality incidents (target zero); share of matters using the approved workflow.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Thomson Reuters CoCounsel (legal research with citations; not verified by an opened source), Microsoft Word Copilot (redlines in the document where lawyers work), Claude (long-contract analysis) and NotebookLM (source-grounded Q&A). Most Specialist hours go to verification, privilege rules and policy design.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit. Word Copilot is narrow but sensible for drafting. Gemini is generic and its enterprise terms need checking. The handbook omits dedicated contract-AI and legal AI platforms such as Harvey, described in a vendor source for diligence (see department 03 source); no opened legal-department source ranks tools, so treat as not verified.

departments.name: Regulatory Compliance
ai_use_cases: Automated regulatory change management: scanning global regulatory sources, identifying relevant changes and mapping obligations to internal policies, risks and controls [1]
Control harmonisation: finding duplicate or overlapping controls across frameworks to reduce testing burden [1]
Dynamic policy mapping against new requirements, highlighting gaps quickly [1]
Co-pilots for compliance research and drafting regulator-ready reports; AI-enabled complaints management (not individually verified) [1]
General counsels and compliance officers using GenAI for compliance workloads: in a CSC survey of 350, 97% had adopted it and 72% had governance policies in place [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A regulatory-change brief for one real recent rule: summary, obligation-to-control mapping table, gap list and a compliance checklist, with citations to the primary regulator text, prompts, a reviewer sign-off, and time saved against a manual baseline. Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Regulator correspondence, examination findings, control evidence, and personal data in monitoring (GDPR); some work touches SOX, PCI DSS, HIPAA or sector rules depending on the firm. Rules: human-in-the-loop review is described by a vendor commentator as a regulatory expectation and responsibility cannot be delegated entirely to AI [1]; be able to show how outputs were produced and validated; cite primary regulatory text, not AI summaries. The claim that regulators are also using AI is not verified.
departments.adoption_kpis: Days from regulation publication to impact assessment; share of obligations mapped to controls; compliance-checklist errors found in review; hours of manual monitoring replaced.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Thomson Reuters CoCounsel (research; not verified by an opened source), Claude and NotebookLM (document-grounded regulatory comparison), and ServiceNow Now Assist if controls evidence sits in ServiceNow. Spend time on audit-ready documentation of AI use.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Fits reasonably. Smaller specialised models were described as more reliable than public models for compliance research [1], so Gemini as a general tool is a weaker fit. The handbook omits dedicated regtech platforms such as 4CRisk.ai, whose COO is the source of the commentary [1] (vendor-sourced).

departments.name: Internal Audit
ai_use_cases: Audit planning: scoping memos, audit announcements, interview guides and background research on business units (interview guides verified; other items not individually verified) [1]
Risk scoring from financial data, operational metrics and prior findings to prioritise audit areas (not individually verified) [1]
Fieldwork: evidence collection linked to test steps and journal-entry anomaly flagging; document extraction and matching from invoices, contracts and GL records not individually verified [1]
Workpapers: converting a recorded walkthrough transcript into a draft walkthrough document for senior review [1]
Continuous auditing: analysing transactional data to flag anomalies near real time rather than at the next cycle [1]
Practical use cases drawn from four audit leaders in the Internal Audit Foundation and AuditBoard report (2024), stressing prompt skills [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: An audit-planning and exception-triage pack for one process (for example procure-to-pay): risk-scored audit universe extract, draft audit programme, a control-test exception list from a supplied sample with each exception traced to evidence, and a draft walkthrough document. Include prompts, a reviewer log of corrections and time saved. Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Financial records and ledgers (SOX), confidential audit findings, personnel data (employment law, GDPR) and fraud indicators. Rules: AI assists but auditors own judgement and evidence; keep an audit trail of prompts and outputs as workpaper evidence; use only secure internal tools for walkthrough recordings [1]. Many internal auditors also lack a clear view of AI use in their own organisation: only 49% of audit leaders in the Optro 2025 Focus on the Future survey (published Nov 2024) reported a clear understanding [3].
departments.adoption_kpis: Hours from walkthrough to draft document; share of engagements using approved AI steps; population coverage versus sample size on tested controls; reviewer correction rate on AI-drafted workpapers.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise AuditBoard AI (the 2025 survey source is published on optro.ai under the Optro name, so check current product naming), Microsoft 365 Copilot, Power BI Copilot for population analysis, and Claude for narrative drafting. Spend the most time on evidence standards and independence.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Fits. Gemini is generic. The survey was published on optro.ai [3], so the handbook's AuditBoard AI label may be out of date (not verified beyond the page). No opened source on omitted tools.

departments.name: Ethics & Investigations
ai_use_cases: Whistleblower response: interpreting complaints, generating follow-up questions and identifying relevant documents [1]
Early-stage triage: identifying and summarising key documents to decide whether a full investigation is needed (not individually verified) [1]
Time-sensitive matters: chronologies, patterns and hot documents to prioritise review (not individually verified) [1]
Detecting anomalous content such as code words or unusual calendar entries in conduct and fraud cases [1]
AI-powered translation inside case management so non-English reports can be investigated without waiting (vendor claim) [2]
Teams are cautiously adopting AI in intake, case management and reporting, per a 2024 benchmarking report [3]
departments.capstone_deliverable: An investigation case file for a synthetic complaint: neutral case summary, evidence timeline, policy-comparison table and list of follow-up interview questions, all with source references. Include a note on what AI was and was not permitted to see (anonymisation step), prompts, human reviewer corrections and time saved. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Whistleblower identities, allegations about named individuals, health and employment data, privileged investigation material. Regulatory hooks: employment law, GDPR, whistleblower protection (the EU Whistleblower Directive and updated US Department of Justice guidance are noted in [2]) and legal privilege. Rules: minimise and pseudonymise data before AI use; AI must not make findings of fact or disciplinary recommendations; human oversight is stressed [1]; model type, jurisdiction and risk profile all affect whether AI is appropriate [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Days to complete case triage; time to build an evidence timeline; share of cases where AI use was documented and reviewed; reviewer correction rate; zero confidentiality breaches.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude and Microsoft 365 Copilot (summaries and timelines inside a secure tenant), ServiceNow Now Assist if cases live in ServiceNow, and a short module on ChatGPT Enterprise only where approved. Spend most time on confidentiality, anonymisation and human decision rules.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: General assistants fit drafting tasks but are a weaker fit for evidence handling than purpose-built investigation or case-management platforms. The handbook omits those (for example Case IQ and Mitratech, the vendors in [2][3]; vendor sources). ChatGPT Enterprise and Gemini need privilege and data-residency review before use on case files.

departments.name: ESG & Sustainability
ai_use_cases: CSRD gap analysis: Ekimetrics' ESG Copilot consolidated data from 20 reports against 1,200+ disclosure requirements, taking 6 weeks instead of about 6 months (vendor case) [1]
Consolidating scattered sustainability data into the CSRD reporting matrix and scoring existing reporting (scoring not individually verified) [1]
Recommendations for remediating data points where reporting does not meet requirements [1]
Drafting ESG report sections and narratives from validated data, with assurance evidence captured at the point of AI output (narrative drafting not individually verified) [2]
Emissions and metric calculations in AI workflows, which must remain traceable under third-party assurance [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A disclosure-gap and narrative pack for three ESRS data points: gap table against supplied source reports, AI-drafted narrative with every figure linked to source, and an evidence log recording model version, inputs, validation and approver. Include prompts and time saved. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Emissions and supplier data, unpublished targets and performance (MNPI for listed firms), and personal data in social metrics (GDPR). CSRD requires third-party assurance of disclosures, so AI workflows need lineage, version history and control evidence [2]. Rules: record model version, source inputs, validation and approval metadata when the metric is created; apply change control to prompts, calculation rules and data-source substitutions [2]; restrict edit and publish rights; avoid generic narrative that does not reflect the firm's actual position. Note: [2] is a community post citing a vendor (Openlayer), so treat as secondary; the current status of CSRD scope and timing should be checked against primary EU sources (not verified).
departments.adoption_kpis: Weeks to complete a disclosure gap analysis; share of reported data points with full lineage; assurance findings related to AI-produced figures; hours spent drafting narrative sections.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude and Gemini (long-document extraction and gap analysis), Power BI Copilot (emissions data narratives) and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Give a dedicated block to assurance and audit trail, since this is the main constraint [2].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Mostly fits. Gamma is a weak fit for the compliance-critical core and only helps with presentation. The handbook omits dedicated ESG data and reporting software; the only example opened is a consultancy's tool (ESG Copilot) [1], so any broader claim is not verified. ChatGPT Enterprise is fine as a general drafter.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: Across the nine departments the dominant pattern is gen AI as a first-draft and synthesis layer (job descriptions, policy answers, feedback and incident summaries, workforce narratives) with a human owning the final decision. The evidence base is mostly vendor and practitioner material: Workday reports a Hackett Group figure that 66% of HR teams use gen AI, but measured outcomes are scarce, so trainees should treat time-saved claims as hypotheses to measure locally. Shared risks are special-category and employee personal data (GDPR), employment-discrimination law, and the EU AI Act and NYC Local Law 144 rules for hiring and worker-management AI, which apply even when a person gives final sign-off. Human reviewers are named as necessary in the payroll and facilities sources; the safety-specific human-review claims (Ibec) could not be verified. Recommended joint training: one common module on employee-data handling, bias testing and human-in-the-loop decisions for departments 11-17 and 19; a second shared lab on HR-knowledge-base prompting for 11, 14, 16 and 18 (employee FAQs, ticket routing); and a safety/facilities pairing for 18 and 19 on incident and work-order summarisation.

departments.name: Human Resources Business Partnering
ai_use_cases: Drafting first-pass answers to common HR inquiries (benefits, leave, payroll, flexible work) from the approved knowledge base, with HR keeping control of final answers [1]
Summarising prior employee cases and conversations so a new HRBP or manager can see history before responding [1]
Producing policy documents, FAQs and manager talking points from HR, legal and compliance input, with human review and sign-off [1]
Summarising multi-source feedback and survey results into themes and recommended actions for HRBPs and leaders [1]
Producing talent-review and workforce summaries for leadership; Gartner-cited data shows 95% of CHROs had adopted AI by end-2025 yet about three-quarters report only moderate or minimal returns [2]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A manager-guidance pack for one live HR topic (e.g. flexible-work requests): a prompt-built policy Q&A of 15 questions answered only from the approved policy text, each answer checked against the source clause, plus a prompt log and a measured before/after drafting time for 10 cases.
departments.data_risks: Employee relations cases hold health, disciplinary, grievance and family data (GDPR special-category data, employment law, possible legal privilege on advice). Rules: no named case data in non-enterprise tools; anonymise before drafting; answer only from approved policy; HRBP verifies against the policy clause before sending; no AI-generated conclusions on individual performance or discipline.
departments.adoption_kpis: Median drafting time per advisory response vs baseline; share of AI-drafted answers sent with zero factual correction; weekly active users in the HRBP team; policy-answer accuracy in a monthly 20-sample audit; rework rate (drafts discarded).

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All eight departments turn structured ledger, bank, spend or contract data into drafts, summaries and exception lists that a named human then reviews, so the shared skill is verification: reperforming numbers, tying output to source and documenting who signed off. Shared risks are confident-but-wrong output, material non-public information, personal and bank data, and weak evidence trails; sources describe COSO's February 2026 generative-AI control guidance and a Workiva finding that 1 in 4 executives said an AI error reached investors or the board. Microsoft itself warns against relying on Copilot in Excel for finance decisions. Training should be joint for a common core (data classification, review gates, prompt and evidence logging) and for three pairings: FP&A, Accounting and Treasury (variance, forecast and close narratives in spreadsheets); AP, Procurement and Vendor Management (P2P documents, contracts, supplier data and fraud signals); and FP&A with Investor Relations (earnings numbers and narrative consistency). Tax and IR need their own legal and disclosure modules.

departments.name: Financial Planning & Analysis
ai_use_cases: Drafting first-pass variance commentary from ledger detail with an LLM; the analyst checks every claim because drafts sound equally confident when wrong [1].

Natural-language questions on planning data inside an FP&A platform (for example 'why did Q2 revenue drop in EMEA?') returning data-backed explanations for monthly business reviews and board books [2].
Running multiple what-if scenarios (inflation, tariffs, supply shifts) on driver-based models in minutes instead of days, with analysts owning assumptions [1][2].
Drafting management reports by department or cost centre against budget from a trial balance, then having analysts add interpretation [3].
Baseline statistical or ML forecasts refreshed each cycle; one source cautions that simple statistical methods have beaten ML in published tests, so baselines are a starting point [1].
departments.capstone_deliverable: A one-month variance pack for a sanitized or synthetic cost-centre dataset: AI-drafted commentary on the top 10 variances, each claim tied to a ledger line, plus a scenario table (base, downside, upside) with stated driver assumptions. Submit the documented prompts, the verification log showing corrections made to AI output, and measured time against a manual baseline. Sized for Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Unreleased results and forecasts are material non-public information for listed companies (securities law, insider-trading and Reg FD exposure). Budgets carry compensation and headcount detail (employment law, GDPR if staff-identifiable). Rules: use only enterprise-licensed tools with no training on inputs, anonymise employee-level data, keep forecast files off consumer tools, keep a human reviewer on any number that leaves finance. Microsoft's Copilot in Excel FAQ says to avoid using Copilot for decisions in sensitive areas such as finance and to verify output [4]. AFP respondents cited data reliability (61%) as a barrier [1].
departments.adoption_kpis: Share of FP&A staff using approved AI weekly (AFP benchmark: 23% use AI daily, weekly or monthly) [1]; hours to produce monthly variance commentary versus baseline; percentage of AI-drafted claims corrected at review; forecast error by horizon before and after; number of scenarios run per planning cycle.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on hands-on variance commentary and scenario work with verification routines, then governance. Prioritise Excel Copilot (where the models live), Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise for narrative and long-document reasoning, and Power BI Copilot for natural-language data exploration. Teach reperformance of every number, because outputs read as authoritative even when wrong [1][4].
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list fits well: Excel Copilot, Power BI Copilot and a general LLM cover the core jobs. Gemini and ChatGPT Enterprise overlap; one general assistant plus the Microsoft tools is enough for most teams (judgment). Omitted: dedicated planning platforms with embedded generative AI, such as OneStream SensibleAI, which offers narrative variance summaries and natural-language questions inside the planning model [2].

Drafting first versions of tax memos, reports and responses to tax authorities for professional review [2].

departments.adoption_kpis: Research hours per query versus baseline; share of AI-cited authorities verified correct; documents processed per hour with extraction accuracy; percentage of GenAI users using it at least weekly (73% of tax-firm and 69% of corporate tax users in the 2025 survey) [1]; whether ROI is measured at all, since only 20% of professionals surveyed do [1].
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend hours on research verification and extraction QA. Prioritise Thomson Reuters CoCounsel (grounded tax research; not verified in opened sources), Claude for long-document reading and memo drafting, and Excel Copilot for scenario and reconciliation work. Teach hallucinated-citation checks first.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit: a research-grade tool such as CoCounsel (not verified in opened sources) with general LLMs for drafting. deptClusters.cluster_overview: All eight departments use AI for the same core jobs: research and synthesis, personalised first drafts, call and meeting summarisation, and reporting on CRM or campaign data. Sellers and marketers also report that data quality, not the model, is the limiting factor (Salesforce: 74% of AI-using sales teams prioritise data hygiene). Shared risks are personal data of prospects and contacts (UK/EU GDPR, PECR or e-privacy marketing consent), recorded-call consent (wiretap litigation against AI notetakers), confidential pipeline, pricing and customer data, and unverified AI claims reaching buyers. Vendor-reported gains are large but self-reported, and independent analyses of ad automation are more mixed, so training should teach measuring incremental results against a baseline. Train together on a common module covering CRM data hygiene, consent and recording rules, citation-checked research and a human review gate before external sending. Sales Ops with the two sales teams, Marketing with Digital Marketing, and Research with BD and Pre-Sales are natural pairings for hands-on labs.

departments.name: Sales - Enterprise & Key Accounts
ai_use_cases: Account and prospect research summarised from CRM, web and internal data; sellers expect agents to cut research time by 34% once fully implemented (survey of 4,050 sellers) [1]
Call summaries, next-step capture and multi-threading checks: Gong Labs found multi-threaded deals over $50K have 130% higher win rates, so AI flags single-threaded deals [2]
Meeting prep and at-risk deal queries in a copilot grounded in CRM, email and decks, e.g. 'a list of deals that are at risk of falling through' [4]
Professional-services firm pilot: early Copilot users reported about 3 hours saved per week, with CRM-based opportunity use cases [3]
Personalised outreach drafts reviewed by the rep; Salesforce reports agents contacted 130,000 leads and created 3,200 opportunities in four months [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: One strategic-account plan for a real or anonymised key account: AI-assisted account brief with every fact linked to a validated source, a stakeholder map flagging single-threaded risk, a call-summary-to-next-steps workflow, a prompt log, and a time-saved comparison (manual vs AI-assisted, minutes per task). Sized for Core-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Customer confidential data, pricing, contract terms and pipeline are commercially sensitive; contact data is personal data under GDPR/UK GDPR. Call recordings need participant consent and notice: AI notetakers face wiretap-law class actions (federal and state wiretapping laws; e.g. Brewer v. Otter.ai, N.D. Cal. 2025) [5]. Rules: use only the enterprise-approved tool, announce recording, no pasting named customer data into consumer chatbots, human review before anything is sent.
departments.adoption_kpis: Weekly active AI users per rep; minutes spent on pre-call research and CRM updates (before vs after); share of opportunities with 3+ buyer contacts; calls recorded with consent notice logged (%); follow-up email turnaround time.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Spend most hours on account research with citation checks, call-summary workflows, and CRM-grounded prompting. Prioritise Salesforce Einstein and Gong AI because they work on the CRM and call data sellers already use; Microsoft 365 Copilot for email and meeting prep; Claude for synthesis. Teach consent and verification explicitly; Gartner-style reinvestment of saved time is a manager topic.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit overall: Einstein, Gong and Copilot match the cited use cases [1][2][4]. Gamma is a weak fit for core selling work (deck output, not research or CRM). Omission: AI meeting notetakers such as Otter and Fireflies are widely used and Otter is the subject of 2025 consent litigation, so the handbook should name the approved recorder and ban unapproved bots [5]. Sales agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot connect to Dynamics 365 and Salesforce, relevant if the firm is on either CRM [4]. Einstein and Gong capabilities beyond the cited pages: not verified.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All five departments turn unstructured customer signals (tickets, calls, surveys, interview notes, feedback, usage data) into summaries, drafts and prioritised actions, and in each one the tool's output is a draft that a human must validate. The shared risks are customer personal data (GDPR/UK GDPR), unapproved "shadow AI" use, and confident but wrong output. Wrong output includes misread sentiment, invented user insight and mis-scored churn risk. Vendor-reported results (resolution rates, retention gains) are marketing claims and should not be used as training benchmarks. Customer Success, Support and CX should train together on voice-of-customer synthesis, data handling and human escalation rules. Product Management and Product Design & UX Research should train together on evidence-grounded PRDs, research synthesis and acceptance criteria. A joint cross-cluster session could use one shared feedback dataset, taking it from support tickets to themes to backlog items.

deptClusters.cluster_overview: All six departments use AI in the same way. An assistant drafts code, tests, infrastructure templates, runbooks or knowledge articles. A human then verifies the draft against something that can pass or fail: a test run, a plan or dry-run, or telemetry. Claude Code's own best-practice guidance says to give the agent a check it can run. Shared risks are source code and credentials pasted into prompts, hallucinated or insecure output, and agents acting with broad permissions on production systems or ERP. Departments 41-44 should train together on agentic coding, verification gates and secrets hygiene, and 43-45 together on cloud and ticket-system tooling. deptClusters.cluster_overview: All five departments sit on sensitive data and on the platforms that hold it, so the strongest pattern is vendor-embedded AI that inherits existing access controls (Security Copilot, Purview, Snowflake RBAC, Power BI semantic models) and works best on well-prepared metadata. Shared risks are over-sharing through broad permissions, unverified AI output feeding decisions (alert verdicts, generated SQL, dashboard answers), and agents taking actions, so human approval gates and evaluation datasets are common requirements. Departments 47 and 48 should train together on SOC and governance handoffs and AI-agent oversight, and 49, 50 and 51 on semantic-layer preparation, answer validation and evaluation-driven development. All five should share one module on governing AI (NIST AI RMF and its generative AI profile) and on data classification. ai_use_cases: Incident and case summarisation inside the service platform to speed handover: not verified (ServiceNow page failed to open).
Incident pattern clustering from ticket exports to find recurring root causes: not verified.
SLA reporting narratives drafted from performance data, then reviewed: not verified.
Knowledge article drafting from resolved tickets: not verified.

Plain-language monitoring of failing jobs and queues (UiPath Autopilot in Orchestrator monitors job health, surfaces failures early and resolves incidents in plain language), relevant for managed automation services. [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: A monthly SLA and incident-pattern review pack from an anonymised ticket extract (at least 200 tickets). It contains an AI-drafted SLA narrative, the top 5 recurring incident themes with validation counts against raw data, and 3 draft knowledge articles. Documented prompts and a time-saved comparison are included. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Tickets carry customer personal data (GDPR), credentials pasted by users, and client-confidential system details covered by contractual confidentiality. Rules: redact personal data and secrets before any non-platform LLM use, keep client data in the contracted tenant, and never let AI-generated SLA figures replace system-of-record calculations (contractual penalties and service credits depend on them).
departments.adoption_kpis: Mean time to resolve; percentage of tickets with AI-generated summary accepted unedited; time to produce monthly SLA report; knowledge-article reuse or deflection rate; AI summary accuracy sampled by QA.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise ServiceNow Now Assist (where tickets live), Power BI Copilot (SLA analytics), and Claude or Gemini (pattern analysis on redacted exports). Spend time on redaction and on validating figures against the system of record.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: The list plausibly fits, but ServiceNow Now Assist capabilities could not be verified because the page failed to open. Omitted but plausible tools such as Jira Service Management/Rovo (the opened Atlassian page covers Jira work-item AI only), Zendesk and Freshservice are not verified.

departments.name: Business Operations & Process Excellence
ai_use_cases: Turning plain-language descriptions into working automations in UiPath Studio via Autopilot, with the vendor claiming 50% faster delivery (vendor claim). [1]
Capturing workflows from live systems and translating business requirements into BPMN designs (Autopilot in Maestro) for process mapping. [1]
Generating tests from requirements and analysing results to keep automation quality high. [1]
Monitoring queues and schedules, surfacing failures early and resolving incidents in plain language. [1]
SOP drafting from process maps or recordings with an LLM: not verified.
departments.capstone_deliverable: One end-to-end process improvement package. It contains an AS-IS process map, an AI-assisted TO-BE design, a draft SOP reviewed against actual practice by a process owner, and an automation or workflow specification. The package includes a documented prompt log and a measured cycle-time or effort estimate. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Process documentation exposes internal controls (relevant to SOX where financial processes are mapped), customer or employee data in sample records, and credentials in recordings. Rules: use synthetic or masked data in prompts, route automations through governed platforms, and require owner sign-off on SOPs. UiPath states Autopilot actions can be recorded through the AI Trust Layer in a GDPR-compliant manner and that Autopilot uses only admin-approved tools [1]; this is a vendor statement, not a compliance guarantee.
departments.adoption_kpis: Number of processes mapped or documented per quarter; SOP drafting time; automations delivered per builder; rework rate of AI-drafted SOPs; percentage of automations built with governed AI assistance.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise UiPath Autopilot and Power Automate (build and governance), Claude (process analysis, SOP writing), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (document and meeting capture). Emphasise validation of AI-drawn maps against observed work.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Good fit; UiPath Autopilot is confirmed as an assistant for building, operating and troubleshooting automations [1]. Gamma is a weak fit (presentation, not process work). Omissions not verified: process-mining and mapping tools (for example Celonis, Signavio); the UiPath page itself lists Process Intelligence and Maestro as related products [1].

departments.name: Business Transformation & Change Management
ai_use_cases: Change impact assessment drafts from project scope documents, validated with stakeholders: not verified.
Tailored change communications by audience segment: not verified.
Synthesis of pulse-survey and feedback comments to find resistance themes: not verified.
Adoption dashboards in Power BI from usage data: not verified.
Stakeholder map and readiness assessment drafts: not verified.
departments.capstone_deliverable: A change package for one realistic initiative. It contains an AI-assisted impact assessment by role, a three-audience communications plan with drafts, an anonymised feedback synthesis with themes traced to source comments, and an adoption KPI plan. It includes a prompt log and a time-saved estimate. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Employee feedback, role-change and restructuring information is personal data under GDPR and employment law (consultation duties). Pre-announcement reorganisations may be MNPI for listed companies. Rules: anonymise and aggregate feedback before AI use, keep restructuring details out of non-enterprise tools, and have HR and legal review communications before release.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to produce an impact assessment; communications issued per audience segment on schedule; stakeholder readiness scores; adoption rate of the new process or tool; share of AI-drafted communications edited before release.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude or ChatGPT Enterprise (analysis and drafting), Microsoft 365 Copilot (documents and email), and Power BI Copilot (adoption analysis). Teach anonymisation and tone and accuracy checks. Gamma and Canva are brief modules.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Broadly fits, but no source was opened, so fit is unverified. Canva and Gamma are comms-production tools and secondary. Omitted tools such as survey platforms (Qualtrics) or digital adoption platforms are not verified.

departments.name: Quality Management & Process Compliance
ai_use_cases: Summarising quality audit findings into trend reports: not verified.
Drafting root-cause analysis (5-Whys, fishbone) from incident records, for human validation: not verified.
SOP revision suggestions by comparing procedure text with audit findings: not verified.
Test-generation and quality validation for automations (UiPath Autopilot in Test Manager generates tests from requirements and analyses results), as an adjacent practice. [1]
Quality KPI narratives from Power BI data: not verified.
departments.capstone_deliverable: A quality review pack from a set of anonymised nonconformance records. It contains an AI-drafted trend summary, root-cause hypotheses each linked to evidence, and a redlined SOP revision with change rationale reviewed by a quality owner. A prompt log and time saved are included. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Quality records can be regulated (ISO 9001, GxP or FDA records in regulated sectors), contain supplier and customer data, and are audit evidence. Rules: AI drafts must not alter controlled records, every AI-assisted change needs a documented human approver, and sensitive product or patient data is excluded from non-approved tools. Specific regulatory citations are not verified.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to compile audit summary; CAPA cycle time; percentage of RCA hypotheses confirmed; SOP review turnaround; error rate found in AI-drafted records.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise Claude (long-document comparison, RCA structuring), Microsoft 365 Copilot (documents), and Power BI Copilot (quality metrics). Focus on evidence tracing and controlled-document rules.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Plausible fit but largely unverified (the only source concerns software-automation testing, not QMS). Gamma is a weak fit for quality records. Omitted: dedicated QMS platforms with AI (for example ETQ, MasterControl): not verified.

departments.name: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
ai_use_cases: Drafting recovery playbooks from system documentation, then validated in exercises: not verified.
Generating tabletop scenario injects: not verified.
Incident communications drafts for staff, customers and regulators: not verified.
Business impact analysis summarisation from interview notes: not verified.
Incident case handling in ServiceNow for continuity events: not verified.
departments.capstone_deliverable: A tabletop exercise kit for one scenario (for example regional data-centre outage). It contains an AI-drafted scenario with timed injects, a recovery playbook section checked line by line against the real architecture, and three pre-approved communication templates. An after-action review is included. Documented prompts and drafting time saved are included. Specialist-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Continuity plans reveal infrastructure weaknesses, recovery credentials, contact details (personal data under GDPR) and critical-supplier dependencies. Resilience regulation such as DORA applies to some financial entities (not verified in a source). Rules: never paste credentials or network diagrams into non-enterprise tools, and treat AI-written recovery steps as untested until exercised. Crisis communications need legal review.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to build a tabletop scenario; playbooks reviewed and refreshed on schedule; exercise issues found per run; communication template readiness; percentage of AI-drafted steps changed in review.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Because the stakes are high, spend hours on verification and exercise design. Prioritise Claude (playbook and scenario drafting), Microsoft 365 Copilot (internal documents), and ServiceNow Now Assist (incident records). ChatGPT Enterprise is secondary.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Unverified: no source opened. Likely gap is dedicated BCM platforms and mass-notification tools, not verified.

departments.name: Supply Chain, Logistics & Inventory
ai_use_cases: Inventory exception review: flagging and explaining stock anomalies from ERP exports: not verified.
Demand insight narratives from planning data: not verified.
Supplier performance reporting drafts: not verified.
SAP Joule queries inside ERP: not verified (the SAP AI assistant page opened but contained no usable product content).
Inventory management appears in UiPath's navigation as a solution area under Manufacturing; this is a vendor listing, not evidence of an AI result. [1]
departments.capstone_deliverable: An inventory exception and supplier report for a masked dataset. It contains an AI-assisted exception list with the top 20 items explained, each reconciled to source data, a draft supplier performance summary, and a prompt and time-saved log. Advanced-tier hours.
departments.data_risks: Supplier pricing and contract terms are commercially confidential (and may raise competition-law concerns if shared), and forecast data can be material non-public information for listed companies. Customs and trade data may be regulated. Rules: use ERP-embedded or enterprise tools, keep supplier pricing out of public LLMs, and have a planner approve any replenishment action.
departments.adoption_kpis: Time to review exceptions; forecast accuracy change (measured versus baseline); stock-out and excess-inventory rate; supplier report turnaround; planner override rate on AI suggestions.
departments.curriculum_emphasis: Prioritise SAP Joule (in the system of record, if the company runs SAP), Power BI Copilot (analysis), and Claude or Gemini (exception explanations on masked exports). Teach reconciling AI narratives to ERP data.
departments.tool_fit_commentary: Unverified: no source supports fit. SAP Joule only fits if the company runs SAP; otherwise it is weak. Omissions such as dedicated planning platforms (for example Kinaxis, o9) are not verified.
